sa.prompt: Explain why performing chin-ups or push-ups might train muscular strength in one individual but muscular endurance in another.
sa.model: Body-weight calisthenics like chin-ups and push-ups use total body mass as the external load. For an unconditioned individual, body weight represents a high relative load (near 1RM), allowing only a few repetitions (<12 reps) and thus training muscular strength. For a well-conditioned athlete with high strength-to-weight ratio, body weight represents a low relative load, allowing 15 to 30 repetitions and effectively training muscular endurance.
criteria: Explain that body weight acts as the external resistance load.
Describe how high relative load limits reps (<12), shifting training to muscular strength.
Describe how low relative load permits 15 to 30 reps, effectively training muscular endurance.
